title: Relief Credit of a Protest Decision — Employer Benefit Charging Adjudication Manual
content:
**Employer Benefit Charging — relief credit of a protest decision.**

The relief credit of a protest decision is the relief reach, less the credits deducted from it, never below zero, times the answer abatement, never more than the charge still standing on the position (every charge posted less every credit posted), rounded to the cent, and it is booked against the single posted charge that still stands within the relief reach.

A protest is an answer given after the notice-of-claim window has closed, so the relief reach takes in no charge already posted, no credit is deducted, the wage-record relief share is zero (0.00), and the answer abatement is one (1.00).

## Order of the calculation

1. Take the relief reach and subtract the credits deducted. A result below zero is taken as zero.
2. Multiply by the answer abatement.
3. Compare with the charge still standing on the position — every benefit charge posted on the position less every credit posted on it — and take the smaller of the two.
4. Round to the cent.

The credit is booked against a single posted charge: the one that still stands within the relief reach.

## Worked example (hypothetical position)

Benefit charges posted on the position total $1,450.00 and credits posted on it total $200.00, so $1,250.00 still stands.

| Step | Working | Figure |
|---|---|---|
| Relief reach less credits deducted | 0.00 less 0.00, not below zero | $0.00 |
| Times the answer abatement | 0.00 multiplied by 1.00 | $0.00 |
| Not more than the charge still standing | the smaller of 0.00 and 1,250.00 | $0.00 |
| Rounded to the cent | | $0.00 |

The relief credit of the protest decision is $0.00.

## Scope

This basis governs only the relief credit of a protest decision; a relief that an appeal decision grants still credits the whole remaining charge of every posting within the relief's scope.
